# Complete browser application assist

## What & Why
The current EscapeHatch artifact is a local-first preparation cockpit, not yet the page-level assistant described in the product vision. It stores a small contact profile, manually maintained answer snippets, and application notes in `localStorage`, but it has no browser extension in this workspace, no resume-to-profile ingestion, no real-form field detection/fill loop, and no reviewed path for turning newly answered application questions into reusable profile knowledge.

Complete the bridge from the cockpit to a browser application-assist surface using the attached two-page resume as the first real intake case. The resume has an extractable text layer and contains the kinds of source material the product needs to handle: contact links, a professional summary, strengths/skills, software/project highlights, multiple roles with dates and bullet points, and education. Import those facts into a reviewable structured profile without placing the user's personal values in source code, test fixtures, logs, or task descriptions.

The assist session must work both as a one-shot page scan and as a controlled multi-page loop. On a page containing all supported fields, it should scan and fill in one explicit action, then clearly tell the user that known fields are populated and that they should review the page and use the site's own Next/Continue control. When the user advances manually, the session should recognize the same-application next page, preserve its state, show that a new page is ready to scan, and wait for the user's explicit fill action. EscapeHatch may report observed page progress, but it must not claim that an application is complete or submitted unless the user explicitly records that outcome.

## Done looks like
- A loadable MV3 browser-assist package exists in the workspace and can be opened while a real or synthetic job application is active.
- The attached resume can be imported locally, parsed, and mapped into an expanded structured profile containing reviewed contact, links, summary, skills, projects, experience, and education data. The user sees the extracted value and source context, can accept/edit/reject each proposal, and invalid or unsupported imports leave the current profile unchanged.
- The user can explicitly start an assist session, inspect the recognized fields and proposed values, fill only approved empty fields, undo the last fill, pause/resume, and latch an emergency stop. Existing values, unknown controls, passwords, uploads, attestations, legal/compliance, demographic, and other policy-sensitive fields remain untouched.
- After a one-shot fill, the extension reports page-level progress such as filled, already populated, manual-review, blocked, and unknown controls, and clearly instructs the user to review the page and advance using the job site's own control. It never clicks Next, Continue, Apply, Submit, or certification controls.
- After manual navigation to another page in the same application origin, the extension preserves the session, detects the new document or SPA form state, shows a ready-to-scan/ready-to-fill status, and waits for explicit user confirmation before writing. It handles repeated pages without losing the fill undo history or confusing one page's results with another's.
- The extension and cockpit can exchange the user's profile and reusable answers through an explicit, validated, user-visible sync flow, with JSON import/export as a recovery path and conflict handling that never silently overwrites newer work.
- After a user manually answers a detected application question, the assist surface can show the question's canonical match and let the user save a reviewed reusable answer or an opportunity-specific override. Unknown or ambiguous questions stay blank and are surfaced for manual mapping; answers are never silently inferred or committed.
- Repeated questions can be suggested from the approved profile/answer library on later application pages, while the user remains responsible for accepting, editing, and submitting the application.
- The cockpit can show an assist session's observed progress and lets the user explicitly record an application milestone. It does not infer “complete” or “applied” merely because all currently visible fields are filled or a page changed.
- The cockpit continues to work without the extension, the current local backup/restore behavior remains compatible, and the extension never requires broad host access or page-runtime network requests.
- Automated coverage exercises the shared mapping/policy logic, resume import validation, sync/conflict behavior, one-shot filling, same-origin multi-page continuation, progress messaging, and a synthetic application flow proving that no submit/continue action is triggered and user-edited values are not overwritten.

## Out of scope
- Automatic clicking of Apply, Next, Continue, Submit, certification, or any other navigation/action control.
- Filling file-upload controls with a resume; browsers require the user to choose files manually. Resume ingestion only extracts reusable facts and suggestions for review.
- Automatic answers for EEO/demographic, work authorization, sponsorship, legal/compliance, compensation, accommodation, truth/accuracy, or other high-stakes questions without the explicit confirmation policy for that question type.
- Treating a route change, a full page, or an empty set of known fields as proof that an application is complete or submitted.
- Accounts, cloud sync, server-side storage, telemetry, or sending profile/resume/application content to the existing API server. The API remains health-only unless a later product decision changes the privacy model.
- Universal compatibility with every ATS framework or custom widget. Unsupported, ambiguous, or inaccessible controls must fail closed and be reported to the user.
- Job-board search, application submission tracking beyond the existing cockpit queue, or redesigning unrelated cockpit persistence features.

## Steps
1. **Define the shared local data contract** — Reconcile the cockpit profile and answer schemas with the browser-assist profile, structured resume sections, canonical question IDs, preference precedence, provenance, freshness, per-application overrides, and page/session progress. Add versioned serialization, migration, validation, and an explicit bridge protocol so sync is user initiated, conflict-aware, and safe to retry.
2. **Build resume-to-profile intake from the attached PDF** — Add a local import flow for the supported document formats, beginning with the attached text-based PDF. Extract only representable facts and answer suggestions, preserve source snippets or page references for review, and present field-by-field confidence/ambiguity states. Persist only approved structured profile/answer data, retain no hidden upload side effects, and preserve the existing workspace when parsing or validation fails. Do not commit the uploaded resume's personal values into source, fixtures, logs, or generated artifacts.
3. **Implement the MV3 assist package** — Port or reimplement the upstream Fill Plan → policy gate → DOM writer pipeline in a workspace-owned browser package. Add active-tab session binding, semantic field classification, live re-gating before every write, exact select matching, existing-value preservation, origin-change pause behavior, page-scoped write batches, and visible Start Assist / Fill This Page / Undo / Pause / Resume / Emergency Stop controls.
4. **Add one-shot and multi-page session state** — Scan all supported controls on the current page in one explicit action, produce a page progress summary, and instruct the user to review and use the site's own Next/Continue action. Observe same-origin full navigations and SPA/DOM changes, preserve the session and per-page history, announce when the next page is ready, and require explicit fill confirmation on each page. Keep application status honest by separating observed page progress from user-recorded completion/submission milestones.
5. **Add reviewed question learning** — Detect visible question prompts and controls beyond the identity/contact lane without guessing their meaning. Match only unambiguous canonical questions, show reusable-answer suggestions with scope and freshness, and provide explicit save/update actions after the user has answered; keep sensitive or unknown questions manual and preserve per-opportunity answers separately from reusable profile knowledge.
6. **Integrate cockpit and extension workflows** — Add the cockpit-side connection/sync entry point, extension-side import/export and status feedback, and a recovery path when the other surface is unavailable. Make profile, resume-derived facts, answer, and session-progress updates visible in both surfaces after a confirmed sync, retain local backups, and surface conflicts with choices rather than silently choosing a side.
7. **Verify the complete user journey** — Add unit/contract coverage for schemas, migrations, resume extraction/review, classification, policy gates, page transitions, fill undo, sensitive-question fail-closed behavior, progress semantics, and conflict resolution. Add browser tests against a synthetic multi-page application fixture for review-before-fill, one-shot fill, explicit next-page guidance, re-scan after manual navigation, no-submit guarantees, manual answer capture, reload/reconnect recovery, and user-edited-field protection; document the load-unpacked setup, supported boundaries, and known ATS compatibility ceiling.
